newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent steadies but August barrels linger.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent steadies but August barrels linger.

text.p: Dated Brent crude steadied in late talk on Tuesday as the first September barrels were offered at higher levels but late August cargoes continued to weigh on the market, traders said.

One of three Sept 3-5 Brents kept ahead of the five o'clock deadline was offered at Sept Brent -10 cents, five cents firmer than the last reported deal on Friday and well above where the August barrels were pegged.
Two Aug 28-31 cargoes were still in the hands of a Wall Street trader, last offered at Oct Brent -35 cents, the equivalent to around Sept Brent -26 cents.
Traders said the uncertainty over the value of the benchmark crude was helping to keep activity on other markets thin.
"Everyone's waiting to see where the next Brent deal will be," said one.
Earlier, cash Brent rallied on news that Venezuela's main export route was closed to tankers after a dredger grounded Monday night in the Lake Maracaibo shipping lane.

Oct Brent rose 27 cents to stand at $19.20 a barrel by 1733 GMT, while intermonth spreads reversed early losses with the prompt Sept/Oct changing hands at -9 cents, up three cents from late Monday levels and Oct/Nov fetching -8 cents, six cents up.
Brent CFDs firmed with the stronger outright levels, next week's dates picking up a couple of cents to talk at Oct Brent -28/-26 cents in thin afternoon discussion.
Other North Sea crudes were steady to a shade higher with first decade barrels, particularly Forties, finding plenty of interest with active trade on Monday.
"It's probably all gone for the first decade now," said a trader.
Details were kept private but traders pegged Forties at around Dated Brent +33/+38 cents.
